pages.title: I- Anatomical reminders

blocks.text: The electrocardiogram represents the electrophysiological investigation which makes it possible to record and analyze the activity of the cardiac bioelectric generators. The electric field created by these generators is complex and varied over time, its origin requires knowledge of certain notions of anatomy. ?The innumerable muscle fibers which constitute the heart are endowed with special properties, the two most important of which are the mechanical power of contraction and the rhythmic electrical activity linked to ionic movements across the membrane. This last property requires a system for distributing nerve impulses to muscle fibers in a certain sequence.

blocks.text: Under normal conditions, the heart is activated from a group of cells forming the sinus node, which, endowed with automatism, itself determines the rhythm of its own excitation. ?The excitation from the sinus node is gradually transmitted to all the atrial fibers then the ventricular fibers via the atrioventricular node, the His bundle and the Purkinje network which extends throughout the ventricular walls. ?This cardiac automatism is under the control of neurovegetative regulations. The arrival of the nerve impulse at the level of the muscular fibers of the heart causes the contraction first of the atria and then of the ventricles. ?The sum of the action potentials emitted in the atria forms the auricular part of the ECG trace; it is the same for the ventricular part

pages.title: II- The action potential of the cardiac fiber

blocks.text: II- The action potential of the cardiac fiber

Like any cell, the cardiac fiber at rest is polarized (resting potential = -90mV). As soon as it is excited, the movement of ions which results from the change of membrane permeability generates an action potential whose essential characteristic is its long duration (100 to 300 ms).

pages.title: Dipolar theory

blocks.text: Two active electrodes placed at both ends of an isolated cardiac muscle fiber and connected to a galvanometer make it possible to record a biphasic trace following the propagation of the action potential along the fiber. The measured value is due to the current which is established between the resting (positive) part and the already excited (negative) part of the cell during depolarization. During repolarization the recorded signal is inverted. The potential difference which appears as soon as the cell enters into activity (depolarization or repolarization in progress) can be represented by a vector dipole of variable amplitude and whose point of application moves: the depolarization vector moves away from the starting point of the excitation and travels parallel to the longitudinal axis of the cardiac fiber. Due to the importance of the duration of the action potential, the cell becomes completely depolarized. The vector which schematizes the repolarization of the fiber evolves in the opposite direction to the depolarization vector.

pages.title: Dipolar theory

blocks.text: So during a complete cycle, a cardiac fiber passes through 04 phases: -Cell at rest (diastolic phase): no ddp is recorded, -Depolarization in progress (start of contraction): the cell being divided into two parts by the depolarization front, a ddp appears between the two electrodes which varies depending on the position of the depolarization front. -Cell entirely depolarized (systolic phase): no ddp is recorded, -Repolarization in progress: a variable ddp appears between the two ends of the cardiac fiber depending on the position of the repolarization front. The cardiac fibers which constitute the atrial myocardium, like those which constitute the ventricular myocardium, contract synchronously and can therefore be compared to a single cell. Thus each of these two large parts of the heart successively undergoes phases of excitation and restoration.

Electric slip theory

blocks.text: A cell membrane can be compared to an electrical sheet because on the one hand, its thickness (e) is very small compared to the distance which separates it from the electrodes and on the other hand, its faces carry a uniform distribution of positive charges on the outside, negative on the inside for a membrane at rest and vice versa for an active membrane. If we call (?) the charge of the leaflet per unit surface, the potential created by the cardiac fiber at a point P distant from it has the expressure Vp = e ?? In this expressure (?) represents the value of the solid angle under which the membrane is seen from the point P. When the cell is at rest, the potential Vp is the sum of the effects of the lower portion ABC and the upper portion ADC. Each of these portions being seen from the same solid angle (?), their contribution to the potential is identical in absolute value but of opposite sign because the sign Vp is that of the face of the sheet which faces P;

pages.title: Electric slip theory
Electric slip theory

blocks.text: When the cell is at rest, P looks at the positive upper side of ADC and the negative inner side of ABC. So a cell at rest gives a zero potential Vp outside. It is the same when the cell is completely depolarized. ?If the contribution to Vp of (?1) and (?3) is zero when the cell is being activated, the same is not true for (?2). ?So for a fixed point P reflecting the position of the electrode, Vp varies in a two-phase manner when the excitation or de-excitation front propagates from one end to the other of the cell.
